(only the lm_head is h2), decode uses packed-half kdot_h2_r1 / kdot_h2q6_r1

comparison_pp_row.units_caveats:
OURS measures ONE batched command buffer that pushes the WHOLE P-token prompt (P = 5 for the pp row) through 24 layers + lm_head, timed by the guest's own SUBMIT fence (GPU only; a fresh process's wall of ~0.41 s includes the 531 MB MAP, warmup and readbacks and is NOT the prompt-processing cost). We report P / step-time in tok/s so the unit is 'prompt tokens per second of batched GPU step'. llama.cpp pp512 = 9135 t/s is engine-timed throughput of a 512-TOKEN prompt batch (0.109 ms/token, weights read once over 512 positions). The two are NOT the same measurement: batch 5 vs 512 positions, GPU-fence vs engine timing, and the selfhost prefill layer kdots are the f32 positions-inner-loop kernel (kdot_f32_p

; the backend's h2 decode layout has no P-row form) while llama.cpp uses its tuned Metal Q8_0 matmul. A llama.cpp 5-token prefill would run near its tg speed (4.23 ms/token), not pp512 speed. The honest statement for the pp row: selfhost batched prefill costs 7.45 ms/prompt-token at P = 5 vs 14.47 ms/token fed one per decode step (1.9x), 5.38 ms/token at P = 8 (2.7x); llama.cpp pp512 is a 512-token batch number and is ~68x lower per prompt token than our P = 5 step, but must not be read as a 5-token prompt latency.

notes.P_parameter:
the generator's standalone prefill mode sizes the batch at P = prompt length and names kdot_f32_p

.spv (PFIX constant), so the 5-token prompt needed kdot_f32_p5.spv (built this tick; spv/ shipped only p4/p8). The requested P = 8 is honored by the second guest: the batch padded to 8 positions with the teacher-forced greedy continuation (314, 746, 600), which is exactly the 8-step run of the decode baseline in ONE batched step and validates all 8 oracle rows.
notes.prefill_colon_P_resident_form_not_used:
prefill:

(iteration 49) is the resident-replay kept-command-buffer form; its ctl ABI takes exactly P tokens per message (P+1 words) so a 5-token prompt cannot ride one message at P = 8, and the resident reply carries no hidden rows for the oracle comparison. The standalone 'prefill' mode is the measured artifact.
notes.fallback_not_needed: 24-layer dense fn-mode prefill compiled and ran; no 64 KiB string-literal refusal (that limit killed prefill-flat at 40 layers -- README tick 41 -- but 'prefill' has been the fn program since tick 42). No 12-layer fallback was required.
